boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Fresno State songs, symbols, ceremonies and recurring events that express Bulldog identity and the university’s connection to the Central Valley.

cards.title: Raise Your Voice for the Alma Mater
cards.subtitle: A 1925 song still heard at Fresno State ceremonies and games
cards.notes: Listen for the alma mater at graduation, the Top Dog Awards Gala or football games, where its performance remains part of the program.
cards.short_summary: Fresno State’s ceremonial song connects present-day gatherings with music written for the university in 1925.
cards.evidence_claim: The Fresno State Alumni Association says the alma mater was written in 1925 and is sung at graduation, the Top Dog Awards Gala and football games.
cards.access_notes: Performances occur during scheduled university ceremonies and athletic events; admission rules depend on the event.

cards.title: Spell Out B-U-L-L-D-O-G-S
cards.subtitle: The fight song ends with a distinctly Fresno State cheer
cards.notes: At an athletic event, listen for the marching band’s fight song and the closing Bulldog spell-out rather than relying on an assumed cue.
cards.short_summary: Adopted in 1934, Fresno State’s fight song turns a band performance into a coordinated Bulldog cheer.
cards.evidence_claim: The Fresno State Alumni Association documents that “Fight Varsity” was adopted in 1934 and is performed by the Bulldog Marching Band at athletic events.
cards.access_notes: The song is heard at scheduled Fresno State athletic events; venue admission and ticket requirements vary.

cards.title: Spot TimeOut in the Crowd
cards.subtitle: Fresno State’s costumed Bulldog has appeared since the 1970s
cards.notes: Look for TimeOut at a public campus or athletic event, and treat any photo opportunity as event-dependent rather than guaranteed.
cards.short_summary: The costumed Bulldog character has served as a recognizable Fresno State event ambassador for decades.
cards.evidence_claim: Fresno State Alumni records that TimeOut debuted in the 1970s and appears at campus and athletic events.
cards.access_notes: Appearances are tied to scheduled campus and athletic events and are not guaranteed at every gathering.

cards.title: Meet the Living Bulldog Tradition
cards.subtitle: A live mascot lineage rooted in a campus encounter from 1921
cards.notes: Watch official channels for Victor E. Bulldog IV appearances; the live mascot’s presence at any particular event should not be assumed.
cards.short_summary: Fresno State maintains a live-Bulldog lineage that traces its inspiration to a white dog welcomed by students in 1921.
cards.evidence_claim: The Alumni Association traces the live-mascot idea to a white bulldog greeted by students in 1921 and identifies Victor E. Bulldog IV as the current successor.
cards.access_notes: Victor E. Bulldog appearances occur at selected official events; consult university announcements before attending.

cards.title: Pass the Collar to the Next Victor E.
cards.subtitle: The president formally transfers live-mascot duties
cards.notes: Treat this as a succession ceremony, not an annual event; revisit university news when a future live-mascot transition is announced.
cards.short_summary: Fresno State marks a live mascot’s succession by placing a ceremonial collar on the incoming Victor E. Bulldog.
cards.evidence_claim: At the 2023 ceremony, Fresno State’s president moved the ceremonial collar from Victor E. Bulldog III to IV to represent the official transfer of duties.
cards.source_title: Victor E. Bulldog IV becomes acting mascot after passing of the collar
cards.access_notes: This ceremony occurs only when the live-mascot role changes; no future date is currently established by the source.

cards.title: Follow the Red Wave’s Road-Trip Origin
cards.subtitle: A fan nickname born from a red-clad journey over Pacheco Pass
cards.notes: Wear red if you join the fan tradition, but check the host venue’s admission, bag and conduct policies before attending any game.
cards.short_summary: The Red Wave name began as a reporter’s description of Fresno State supporters traveling together to San Jose.
cards.evidence_claim: Fresno State credits journalist Ron Orozco with coining “Red Wave” after seeing hundreds of red-clad Bulldogs fans travel to San Jose in 1981.
cards.source_title: How the Red Wave was Born
cards.access_notes: Participation centers on Fresno State athletic events; tickets and venue policies vary by contest.

cards.title: Find the Green V on a Bulldog Helmet
cards.subtitle: One green letter carries the San Joaquin Valley connection
cards.notes: Look at the back or sides of current football helmets for the Green V, then compare it with the mark used elsewhere in Fresno State Athletics.
cards.short_summary: The Green V visually links Bulldog athletics to the Central Valley and its agricultural heritage.
cards.evidence_claim: Fresno State Athletics says the Green V symbolizes the university’s connection to the San Joaquin Valley, with green honoring regional agriculture.
cards.source_title: The meaning of the Green V
cards.access_notes: The symbol is visible through official athletics imagery and at scheduled sporting events; event admission varies.

cards.entity_name: Bulldog Marching Band Dog Tag Ceremony
cards.title: Earn a Bulldog Band Dog Tag
cards.subtitle: Band camp ends with a necklace and a formal welcome
cards.notes: Attend only if the band announces a public rehearsal; receiving a dog tag is reserved for members who complete Bulldog Marching Band camp.
cards.short_summary: A post-camp ceremony welcomes each Bulldog Marching Band member with an identifying dog-tag necklace.
cards.evidence_claim: The Collegian reports that the ceremony has occurred annually since 2015 and gives every band member a dog tag after completing band camp.
cards.source_title: Precision in practice: A sneak peek into the Bulldog Marching Band’s preseason rehearsals
cards.access_notes: The ceremony is for band members; public observation depends on the band’s current rehearsal announcement.

cards.title: Spend a Spring Weekend at Vintage Days
cards.subtitle: A student-run Fresno State festival dating to 1975
cards.notes: Check the current Vintage Days schedule before visiting, then choose among the crafts fair, performances, Kids Zone and student booths.
cards.short_summary: Vintage Days turns campus into a multiday spring festival planned by students and shared with the wider Fresno community.
cards.evidence_claim: Fresno State documents Vintage Days as a student-run tradition begun in 1975; the 2026 edition featured crafts, performances and all-ages attractions.
cards.source_title: Fresno State Campus News | Vintage Days 2026
cards.access_notes: Vintage Days is a scheduled spring event. Some attractions or food require payment even when campus admission is free.

cards.title: Find a Campus Community at Traditions Day
cards.subtitle: The fall tradition is Fresno State’s largest club fair
cards.notes: Go during the second full week of fall classes, speak directly with club representatives and confirm current participation details before joining.
cards.short_summary: Traditions Day concentrates Fresno State’s student organizations into a recurring early-semester introduction.
cards.evidence_claim: Fresno State Student Involvement identifies Traditions Day as its largest club and organization fair and places it in the second full week of fall semester.
cards.access_notes: This recurring fall event is campus-focused; consult Student Involvement for the current date and participation rules.
